EIA FORECAST (Sept 9, 2026 STEO): US retail regular averages $3.84/gal in 2026 and $3.35/gal in 2027. Wholesale gasoline goes from $3.11 to $2.39. Brent averages $91.01/b in 2026 and $73.74/b in 2027. EIA expects the Strait of Hormuz constraints to last through 4Q26, with Middle East output near pre-conflict levels by 2Q27. Sources: https://finance.yahoo.com/sectors/energy/articles/eia-raises-usa-fuel-price-165930520.html ; https://www.rigzone.com/news/eia_raises_usa_fuel_price_projections_for_2026_2027-17-apr-2026-183480-article/ ; https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/steo/pdf/steo_text.pdf ; https://truedrivingcost.com/articles/gas-price-forecast-2026-2027
- EIA has repeatedly revised its 2027 forecast: Feb $2.93, Mar $3.18, Apr $3.46, Sep $3.35. Actual late-Sept prices ($4.48 national) are already well above the Sept STEO path, so the forecast is highly uncertain.

winter_notes:
All figures in this section are ESTIMATES or general knowledge; none came from sources retrieved this session.
- Snow: Madison averages roughly 50 inches of snow a year (NWS normal, from memory) and gets frequent sub-zero nights from Dec to Feb. City arterials are plowed and salted well; side streets and apartment lots are the problem.
- AWD vs FWD: A FWD Toyota or Lexus on real winter tires handles Madison fine. AWD helps you start moving and climb hills but does not help braking or cornering. Tires matter more than drivetrain. RWD cars (IS 250/350 and GS 350 RWD) on all-season tires are poor in snow; only buy one if you also buy winter tires. AWD does matter for resale: AWD RAV4, RX, and Highlander sell faster and for more in Wisconsin, which helps when selling in Aug 2027. AWD costs about 1-2 mpg.
- Winter tires (estimates): 4 tires only (15-17 inch sedan or hybrid, e.g. Blizzak or X-Ice): about $500-900, plus mount/balance about $80-150 each season change. Tire-and-steel-wheel package (16-17 inch): about $800-1,200. SUV 18-19 inch package (RX, Highlander, Evoque): about $1,100-1,800. Land Rover LR4 or RRS needs 19-inch or larger wheels to clear the brakes: about $1,600-2,500+. Used winter sets on Facebook Marketplace or Craigslist often go for 30-50% of new. A car that already comes with a winter set is worth about $400-800 extra to you. You can resell the set in spring 2027 or sell it with the car.
- Rust: Wisconsin road salt is harsh. Inspect rocker panels, wheel arches, subframes, brake and fuel lines, and frames on body-on-frame trucks (4Runner, GX 470). Cars that lived in southern states cost more but resell better; ask for a Carfax. Oil-based undercoating (Fluid Film or Krown type) costs about $100-200/yr. Wash the underbody regularly in winter. Pay about $100-200 for a pre-purchase inspection.
- 12V battery: Cold kills weak batteries. If the battery is older than 4-5 years, replace it right away (about $150-250 for a conventional battery, $250-400 for AGM on Land Rover or some Lexus). Prius and CT 200h 12V auxiliary batteries run about $200-300. Keep jumper cables or a jump pack. A block heater is usually not needed.
- Hybrid traction battery replacement (estimates): Prius Gen 3 (2010-2015) new OEM about $2,500-3,500 installed, reconditioned about $1,200-2,000. CT 200h (same system) about $2,500-3,800 dealer, $1,500-2,200 reconditioned. ES 300h (2013-2018) about $3,000-4,500 dealer, $2,000-2,500 reconditioned. RX 450h (2010-2015) about $3,500-6,000 dealer, $2,500-3,500 reconditioned. Factory hybrid warranty (8yr/100k on these years) has expired on all of them. A hybrid battery health check (e.g., Dr. Prius app with an OBD dongle, or a shop test) is essential before buying. Cold weather cuts hybrid winter mpg by roughly 15-30%.
summary:
Fuel (verified): Madison regular was $4.03 on Sept 14, 2026 and $4.46 on Sept 21 (Stacker). The Wisconsin AAA average was $4.34 on Sept 17 and $4.36 on Sept 25. Nationally on Sept 28, regular was $4.48 and premium $5.36, a gap of about $0.89. I found no Madison premium figure; my estimate is about $5.30-5.40. EIA's Sept 9 STEO forecasts US regular at $3.84 for 2026 and $3.35 for 2027, but prices are running well above that path because of Iran and Hormuz. My planning estimate for Oct 2026-Aug 2027 is about $3.80 regular and $4.70 premium.

Tooling limit: WebSearch hit its session cap (200/200) after the fuel and ES 350 queries. So the per-model EPA MPG, fuel grades (except the ES 350), RepairPal averages, winter tire prices and battery costs come from memory and general knowledge. They are labeled ESTIMATE or unverified and should be checked on fueleconomy.gov and RepairPal. Only the 2011 ES 350 figures (22 combined, 19/27) and its fuel grade were confirmed by search: 2007-2010 recommends premium but allows 87, and 2011-2012 uses regular.

Fuel for 9,000 miles (estimate): Prius about $684; CT 200h about $814; ES 300h or Camry Hybrid about $855; Corolla about $1,100-1,180; Camry 4-cyl about $1,221; RAV4 about $1,315-1,368; 2011-12 ES 350 about $1,555 on regular; RX 350 about $1,630-1,710; IS or GS on premium about $1,840-2,015; GX 470 about $2,820; LR4 or RRS V8 about $3,000-3,250.

Maintenance and repair per year for 10-15 yr old cars (estimate): Corolla, Camry, RAV4, Prius about $500-800. ES, Avalon, Highlander, 4Runner about $600-1,000. RX, IS, GS about $800-1,300. GX 470 about $1,000-1,500. Land Rover about $1,500-4,000+, with single repairs of $1,000-6,000 (air suspension, 5.0 timing chain).

Conclusion for a 10.5-month ownership: Land Rovers are the worst value. They cost the most in fuel (premium at about 14 mpg), have the highest repair risk, and depreciate steeply at resale. The best value is a 2011-2012 ES 350 (runs on regular, reliable) or an AWD RAV4 or RX 350 (strong Wisconsin resale). A Camry, Corolla or Prius is the lowest-cost choice. Budget $800-1,500 for winter tires and wheels on any car, and more on a RWD car.
